overall_summary: Space and exoplanet mysteries, particularly those featuring extreme planetary conditions or 'What If' survival scenarios, are driving the highest views and engagement. Meanwhile, repetitive psychology and brain facts are underperforming and struggling to capture audience interest.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'The Planet of Burning Ice Will Break Your Brain!' (1,055 views) and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,025 views) represent the channel's peak performance.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on extreme cosmic environments, focusing on bizarre weather, extreme temperatures, and terrifying planetary traits.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' achieved 946 views and 'What If You Fell Into This $26 Nonillion Diamond Planet?' hit 492 views.
winning_patterns.action: Frame cosmic facts as hypothetical survival scenarios, placing the viewer directly into the extreme environment to boost retention.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' repeatedly flopped with views as low as 5 to 10, and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' only got 17 views.
weak_patterns.action: Pause generic cognitive psychology facts and pivot those resources toward high-performing space and animal survival niches.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'How Do Clouds Float If They Weigh THIS Much?' stalled at 77 views.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid passive, textbook-style questions; replace them with high-stakes, active hooks.

next_video.reason: Leverages the highly successful 'What If You Fell...' format combined with extreme planetary weather (HD 189733b), matching the 21-second duration of our best-performing space videos.
